_note: Geometry for the schematic map of the project. Tunnel routes are drawn smoothly from point to point: no alignment has been studied. Corridor lengths are planning estimates read from maps; the four approach corridors end where the tunnels come up on the existing tracks, at the ring road (east: at Rosa Parks, just inside it); RER F comes up near Pont-Cardinet; the link is 5 km (4.5 to 6). Each corridor lists the tunnels that run in it (tgv, n, h), as model.tunnels.corridors. There is no regional express tunnel (version 4.1): every TGV tunnel is a TGV + TER tunnel, open to the regional express trains, the TGVs having priority. The corridors where the peak timetable runs regional express trains have a 'ter' key (the load key in model.ter_paths.loads, as model.ter_corridors); the link has none in the timetable but a 'carries.ter' text all the same. The Seine and the existing lines are sketched by hand for orientation. 'today' lists today's suburban lines that the RER tunnels take over (net: n for RER G, h for RER F), from their portal outwards: the main paths follow the existing lines above; the branches marked 'schematic' are approximate, drawn by hand for orientation; 'lbl' places the line's letter: share of the way along the path, and side (1 or -1).

stations.name: Paris Nord-Est
stations.where: Under and between Gare du Nord and Gare de l’Est, which are 500 m apart.
stations.calls: TGVs of all four lines stop here, from the north, the east, the south-east and the Atlantic; one of the six TGV tracks can be closed off for each London departure. Regional express trains run through in the TGV + TER tunnels: those from the north on to Montparnasse and the Atlantic lines, those from the east on to Gare de Lyon and Burgundy. Their four platforms lie on the west side of the box, beside the TGV platforms. RER G from the east runs through to Montparnasse, and RER F from the north runs on to Saint-Lazare.
stations.surface: Every train of Gare du Nord and Gare de l’Est goes underground, so all the surface tracks of both stations are freed: both halls become entrances, and the platforms and approach tracks become one park.
stations.under: under Gare du Nord and Gare de l’Est
stations.stage_note: TGV and RER F platforms in stage 1; regional express and RER G platforms in stage 2.

stations.name: Gare de Lyon
stations.calls: TGVs of the south-east, and the half of the northern, eastern and Atlantic TGVs that pair with them; regional express trains of Burgundy, running through in the TGV + TER tunnel to Nord-Est and the east. Two of the eight tracks, one each way, take the planned sixteenth south-eastern TGV an hour and the regional express trains. A junction at the city end leads to the direct link to Montparnasse.
stations.surface: The hall is kept as the entrance. The TGVs and the regional express trains go underground and the Bercy station is freed. Line R keeps a small terminal of a few surface tracks; running it through as well is left as a later option.
stations.tgv_note: two of them, one each way, also take the regional express trains

stations.name: Montparnasse
stations.calls: TGVs of the Atlantic, and the half of the northern, eastern and south-eastern TGVs that pair with them; regional express trains of the Chartres, Le Mans and Granville lines, running through in the TGV + TER tunnel to Nord-Est and the north; RER G running through to Nord-Est. A junction at the city end leads to the direct link to Gare de Lyon.
stations.surface: Every train goes underground. The hall is kept as the entrance; the surface tracks towards the ring road become a park.

stations.name: Saint-Lazare
stations.where: Deep under the present station, a new through station for RER F only.
stations.calls: RER F only: trains from the north (today’s lines H and K) run through Nord-Est to here, then back up onto the Batignolles tracks at Pont-Cardinet and on to the branches of line L, which become further branches of RER F. The point is less Saint-Lazare itself, which RER E already serves, than a ride without a change from the northern suburbs to Pont-Cardinet, Clichy-Levallois, Courbevoie and La Défense.
stations.surface: The surface station stays as it is, for line J and the Normandy trains: no park here, and no new hall.

stations.name: Châtelet-Les Halles
stations.where: Under the Forum des Halles, beside the station of RER A, B and D.
stations.calls: RER G only, a stop in passing between Nord-Est and Montparnasse: its riders change here to RER A, B and D and metro lines 1, 4, 7, 11 and 14. One platform track each way: RER A takes up to 30 trains an hour on one track each way at Auber and Châtelet.
stations.surface: Nothing changes on the surface but new exits into the Forum des Halles.

junctions.name: Northern junction
junctions.what: Where the TGV + TER tunnels from the north and from the east become one, just before the station. The regional express trains of both lines ride in these TGV + TER tunnels and need no cavern of their own. RER F comes from the north only and RER G from the east only, so they need no junction.

junctions.name: Southern junction
junctions.what: Where the TGV + TER tunnels to Gare de Lyon and to Montparnasse part, just after the station; the regional express trains from the north take the Montparnasse side, those from the east the Gare de Lyon side. RER G runs on to Montparnasse only, and RER F turns west to Saint-Lazare, so they need no junction.

junctions.name: Montparnasse junction
junctions.what: Where the direct link to Gare de Lyon leaves the TGV + TER tunnel from Nord-Est, at the city end of Montparnasse. Its geometry has not been designed.

junctions.name: Gare de Lyon junction
junctions.what: Where the direct link from Montparnasse joins the TGV + TER tunnel from Nord-Est, at the city end of Gare de Lyon. Its geometry has not been designed.
